info.title: Finn API
info.summary: Create voice agents, place calls, read and update CRM records, start Finn Operator cases and decide approvals.
info.description:
The Finn API is a REST API for building on Finn voice agents ("Finns"): create and configure Finns, rent phone numbers, upload audiences, start inbound and outbound deployments, place single calls, read call results and the wallet ledger, and receive a signed `call.completed` webhook when each call ends.

The API is in **beta**. Every operation here is live; shapes can still change before general availability.

## What this API covers
This API covers Finn's voice agents (scopes `voice:read`, `voice:write`), CRM records (Records), and Finn Operator cases and approvals (Cases, Approvals), and the chat inbox (Chat, beta: switched on per organization). AI assistants can also reach Finn agents and the CRM through the [MCP server](https://www.hirefinn.ai/docs/mcp).

## Getting started
1. Create an API key in the dashboard under **Settings → Integrations → API keys**.
2. Pick a voice with `GET /voices`.
3. Create a Finn with `POST /finns` (`name` and `voice` are required).
4. Place a test call to your own phone with `POST /calls`, or create an audience with `POST /audiences` and start an outbound deployment with `POST /deployments` from a number listed by `GET /phone_numbers`.
5. Add a webhook endpoint in the dashboard to receive `call.completed` after each call, and read any call with `GET /calls/{call_uuid}`.

The step-by-step version with full requests is the [API quickstart](https://www.hirefinn.ai/docs/api-quickstart).

## Authentication
Send an API key as a bearer token: `Authorization: Bearer finn_live_...`. Create and revoke keys in the dashboard under **Settings → Integrations → API keys**; there is no API for managing keys. Each key belongs to one organization and reaches only that organization's data, limited by the key's scopes. Scopes are `product:access` (`voice:read`, `crm:write`, `operator:read`, `approvals:write`...; `chat:read` and `chat:write` are for the separate Chat API); the names keys were made with before (`voice`, `cases:read`, `cases:write`, `dnc:write`) still work and mean what they did. A new key gets `voice` (read and write) unless you pick others; a key made before scopes existed keeps what it had. A missing scope returns `403 insufficient_scope`. See the `ApiKey` security scheme and [scopes](https://www.hirefinn.ai/docs/api-scopes). Every key is live: there is no sandbox, so calls are real and billed.

Call the API from your server. A request carrying a browser `Origin` that Finn does not allow is rejected with `403 origin_not_allowed`.

## Requests and responses
Request bodies are JSON (`Content-Type: application/json`, at most 10 MB). Successful responses have the shape `{ "success": true, "data": ... }`; list endpoints add `limit` and `offset`. Records, Cases and Approvals don't use this envelope: they return the object itself (for example `{ "contact": ... }`). IDs are UUIDs, timestamps are ISO 8601 and phone numbers are E.164 where noted. A resource in another organization returns `404`, the same as one that does not exist.

## Errors
Errors return an HTTP status and `{ "error": "<code>", "message": "..." }`. Check `error`, not `message`. `internal_error` has no `message`. Errors that need action in the dashboard (compliance, billing, API keys) include an `action_url`.

A few failures happen before an endpoint runs and use a different shape: a body that is not valid JSON returns `400` with `{ "success": false, "error": "<parser message>" }` (even without a key), a body over 10 MB returns `413`, and an unknown path returns `404` with `{ "success": false, "message": "..." }`.

## Rate limits
Limits are counted per API key in fixed 60-second windows, per endpoint group, and shared across all of Finn's servers; each operation lists its limit. Responses carry `RateLimit-Policy`, `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining` and `RateLimit-Reset` (seconds until the window resets). Over the limit returns `429 rate_limited` with `Retry-After`; nothing was done, so it is safe to retry after waiting.

## Pagination
List endpoints take `limit` and `offset` and return no total count (except audience contacts and the do-not-call list). Keep requesting with a larger `offset` until a page returns fewer than `limit` items. Records use `page` and `page_size`; cases use `before`; approvals use `cursor`.

## Retries
The writes that spend money (`POST /calls`, `POST /deployments`, `POST /deployments/inbound`, `POST /phone_numbers`) and starting a case accept an `Idempotency-Key` header (Chat sends require one): a retry with the same key and body returns the first response instead of doing the work twice. Other writes are not idempotent; check state before retrying them after a timeout or a `5xx`.

## Webhooks
Add webhook endpoints in the dashboard under **Settings → Integrations → Webhooks**; there is no API for managing them. See the `call.completed` webhook for the signature and retry behaviour; `contact.updated`, `case.created`, `case.completed` and `approval.requested` are also described here. The full list of 14 events is in [webhook-events](https://www.hirefinn.ai/docs/webhook-events).

post.description:
Places one outbound call with a Finn. The Finn supplies the voice, prompt, language, transfer number and call flow; you supply the destination.

If the Finn's `call_flow` is turned on, the call runs it with its tools (end call, call transfer, Cal.com booking), as deployment calls do. The call uses the Finn's `system_prompt` (added after `identity_text`) but not `max_call_duration_minutes`, `idle_reminder_message`, `idle_reminder_after_seconds` or `end_call_on_silence_seconds`: those apply only to calls from deployments, and a single call runs with Finn's defaults for them.

The response is `202 Accepted` once the call has been accepted for dialing. It does not mean anyone answered: the outcome arrives later on the call record (`GET /calls/{call_uuid}`) and in the `call.completed` webhook.

Calls placed with this endpoint use a Finn-managed caller ID that you cannot choose. To call from a number you rent, or to call a list of contacts, create an outbound deployment instead.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header so a retry after a timeout or a `5xx` returns the first response instead of placing a second, billed call. Without the header, retrying a request that reached the server places a second call.

**Rate limit:** 60 requests per minute per API key.

get.description:
Returns any call in your organization: calls placed with `POST /calls`, calls dialed by deployments and inbound calls.

The record appears shortly after the call ends, so a lookup right after a call can return `404 call_not_found` for a few minutes; retry with backoff or wait for the `call.completed` webhook. `analysis` stays empty until post-call analysis has run.

`billing` is an estimate computed when you read the call (`ceil(duration_seconds / 60)` credits at your current rate). The wallet ledger (`GET /wallet/transactions`) is the record of what was charged.

**Rate limit:** 300 requests per minute per API key, shared with `GET /calls/{call_uuid}`, `GET /finns`, `GET /finns/{finn_id}` and `GET /wallet`.

Includes the transcript and the analyzer's summary and scores. Both are null until the
respective job has run, so a call that has only just finished is still a valid response.

post.description:
Creates a Finn with status `draft`. It does not place or answer calls until you deploy it (or place a single call with it). Only `name` and `voice` are required.

`voice` must be a voice your organization can use, from `GET /voices`; the Finn is put on that voice's provider. Speech-to-text and the language model are set by Finn and are not part of the API. Set the call flow, including the built-in end call, call transfer and Cal.com tools, with `call_flow`. Add knowledge base documents with `POST /finns/{finn_id}/knowledge_base`. Variables are configured in the dashboard.

`max_call_duration_minutes`, `idle_reminder_message`, `idle_reminder_after_seconds` and `end_call_on_silence_seconds` apply to calls from deployments only; calls placed with `POST /calls` run with Finn's defaults for them.

The Finn is attributed to the user who created the API key. A retried create makes a second Finn.

**Rate limit:** 60 requests per minute per API key, shared by `POST`, `PATCH` and `DELETE` on Finns.

get.description:
Lists the voices your organization can give a Finn.

Pass a `voice_id` from here as `voice` when you create or update a Finn. **That is the only voice field there is** — the TTS provider is not part of the API and must not be sent. It is derived from the voice ID, whose format is unambiguous:

| Provider | `voice_id` format | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Cartesia (default) | UUID, hyphenated | `f786b574-daa5-4673-aa0c-cbe3e8534c02` |
| ElevenLabs | alphanumeric, no hyphen | `FGY2WhTYpPnrIDTdsKH5` |

Cartesia is the platform default and is listed first, so it is what you get unless you deliberately pick an ElevenLabs voice.

Narrow the list with `language` (a name such as `Hindi` or a code such as `hi`; region subtags match, so `en` also matches `en-IN`), `search`, and `limit`/`offset`. `total` is the count after filtering, before paging.

If one provider's catalog can't be loaded, the response still succeeds with the other provider's voices. If neither can be loaded, it returns `502 voices_unavailable`.

**Rate limit:** 60 requests per minute per API key, shared by `GET /voices` and `GET /voices/{voice_id}`.

parameters.description: Only voices that speak this language. Accepts a name (`Hindi`, `English`) or a code (`hi`, `en`, `en-IN`). Region subtags match in both directions, so `en` matches `en-IN` and `en-IN` matches `en`. `Hinglish` matches Hindi and Indian-English voices, since Hinglish is code-switched.

post.description:
Rents a number found with `GET /phone_numbers/available`. **Your wallet is debited when the request is accepted.** The carrier purchase then runs in the background: the response has no `id`, so poll `GET /phone_numbers` until the number appears. If the purchase fails, the debit is refunded and the number never appears.

Requires an approved compliance application (completed in the dashboard). The rental is attributed to the user who created the API key, who must still be a member of your organization with an email on record. post.description:
Sent once per call to each webhook endpoint after the call ends, answered or not: calls from outbound and inbound deployments and calls placed with `POST /calls`. If the Finn has a **Data webhook URL** (set in the dashboard under the Finn's **Deployment settings**), that URL also receives the event, signed with the Finn's own secret.

Unanswered calls, and calls on a Finn without analysis questions, are usually sent within about 5 minutes. For an answered call on a Finn with analysis questions, the event waits for the analysis, so `analysis` is normally filled in; if analysis has not arrived after about an hour, the event is sent with what exists. New endpoints are not backfilled with older calls.

**Verify the signature.** `X-Finn-Signature` is `t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex>`, where `v1` is the HMAC-SHA256 of `<t>.<raw request body>` keyed with the whole signing secret, including its `whsec_` prefix, as UTF-8. Compute it over the raw body bytes before parsing JSON, compare in constant time, and reject timestamps older than a few minutes.

**Delivery and retries.** Endpoints must use `https` and resolve to a public address. Each attempt times out after 10 seconds, and redirects are not followed. Any `2xx` response marks the event delivered. Timeouts, connection errors, `429`, `5xx`, `3xx` and responses larger than 64 KB are retried, up to 3 attempts in total (waiting 1 second, then 2 seconds). Other `4xx` responses are not retried. Each endpoint gets at most one `call.completed` per call; after 3 failed attempts the event is not sent again, so reconcile with `GET /calls/{call_uuid}`. De-duplicate on `call_uuid`.

**Durable delivery.** When your organization has durable webhooks switched on (ask Finn support), `call.completed` goes through the same queue as record events: it survives a Finn restart, carries `event_id` (`call.completed:<call_uuid>`), `occurred_at` and `org_id`, goes out in order with the endpoint's other events, and a send that failed with a timeout, connection error, `429` or `5xx` is tried again after 1 min, 5 min, 30 min, 2 h and 6 h. `recording_url` is signed when the event is sent and is valid for one hour. An endpoint with 30 failed sends in a row and no success for a day is switched off (`enabled: false`); `GET /webhook_endpoints/{id}/deliveries` shows what happened.

TestApiKey.description:
A **test key**, starting with `finn_test_`, made in a practice organization (Settings → Integrations → API keys → Test key). It carries scopes like a live key and is sent the same way (`Authorization: Bearer finn_test_…`). Reads, writes and agent runs act on the practice organization for real, but nothing reaches a customer or spends credit: placing a call, renting a number, starting a deployment and sending a chat message return `403 test_mode`, and anything else outbound is blocked by practice mode.

Test keys exist only where Finn has turned them on for your organization. A test key whose organization is no longer a practice organization returns `401 test_key_not_allowed`; one whose organization has test keys turned off returns `401 test_keys_not_enabled`.

ApiKey.description:
An API key starting with `finn_live_`, created in the dashboard under **Settings → Integrations → API keys**. A missing key, or a token without the `finn_live_` prefix, returns `401 api_key_required`; an unknown or revoked key returns `401 invalid_api_key`.

Each key carries **scopes** that decide which endpoints it may call. A scope is `product:access`; the products are `voice`, `chat`, `crm`, `operator`, `approvals`, `sales`, `dialer` and `admin`.

| Scope | Allows |
|---|---|
| `voice:read` | Read calls, Finns, voices, phone numbers, audiences, deployments, wallet and the do-not-call list: every `GET` tagged Calls, Finns, Voices, Phone numbers, Audiences, Deployments, Wallet or Do not call. |
| `voice:write` | Every other method on those endpoints: place calls, create and change Finns, rent numbers, upload audiences, deploy, add do-not-call numbers. |
| `voice:dnc:write` | Remove a number from the do-not-call list. |
| `crm:read` | Read records, record kinds, fields and a record's timeline. |
| `crm:sensitive:read` | See the values of fields marked sensitive. Without it they come back as `{ "redacted": true, "set": true|false, "hint"? }`. |
| `crm:write` | Create and update records, add notes. |
| `operator:read` | Read Finn Operator cases and their events. |
| `operator:write` | Start a case. |
| `approvals:read` | Read pending approvals. |
| `approvals:write` | Approve or reject a pending approval. |
| `chat:read` | Read chat channels, conversations, messages and chat contacts. |
| `chat:write` | Start conversations, send messages, update chat contacts. |
| `admin:webhooks` | Create, read, change and delete webhook endpoints, read their deliveries and the event list (`/webhook_endpoints`, `/events`). Never given to a key unless picked, nor to a key made before scopes. |

`operator:build`, `sales:read`, `sales:write`, `dialer:read`, `dialer:write`, `admin:read` and `admin:write` are reserved: a key may carry them, and no endpoint checks them yet.

A write scope includes the read it builds on: `voice:write` includes `voice:read`; `voice:dnc:write` includes `voice:write`; `crm:write` and `crm:sensitive:read` include `crm:read`; `operator:write` includes `operator:read`; `approvals:write` includes `approvals:read` and `operator:read`; `chat:write` includes `chat:read`.

**Older scope names** still work and mean exactly what they did:

| Older name | Same as |
|---|---|
| `voice` | `voice:read` + `voice:write` |
| `dnc:write` | `voice:dnc:write` |
| `cases:read` | `operator:read` + `approvals:read` |
| `cases:write` | `operator:write` |

Pick scopes when you create the key; a new key with none picked gets `voice`. A key created before scopes existed keeps the access it had: every scope above except `voice:dnc:write`, `approvals:write` and the reserved ones. A request without the scope it needs returns `403 insufficient_scope` with `required_scope`. Each operation names its scope in its description and in `x-required-scope` (and the older name in `x-legacy-scope`).

AI agents should use a key with only the scopes they need.

post_call_analysis.description:
Questions answered automatically after each call. Up to 50.

Four question types, all shown in the example:

- `Yes/No` — a boolean judgement.
- `Selector` — one of `choices`. Supply `choices`, or the analyzer has nothing to pick from.
- `Number` — a numeric answer.
- `Text` — free text; use `formatExamples` to steer the wording.

Read the answers per call with `GET /calls/{call_uuid}` (`analysis`), or aggregated
across the Finn with `GET /finns/{finn_id}/post_call_analysis`.

name.description: Display name, 1 to 255 characters after trimming.

IdempotencyKey.description: Your unique key for this request, 1 to 255 visible ASCII characters (a UUID works well). A retry with the same key and the same body within 24 hours returns the first response instead of doing the work again. See [api-idempotency](/docs/api-idempotency).

FinnVersion.description: Pins the API version for this request, a date such as `2026-11-01`. Overrides the version pinned on the API key; without either, the current version is used. An unknown version returns `400 invalid_finn_version`. Honoured only while version pinning is switched on (beta); otherwise ignored.

FinnOrg.name: Finn-Org
FinnOrg.description: The organization this request acts in (its id). An OAuth token (`finn_oat_`) or personal MCP key (`finn_mcp_`) that can act in more than one organization must name one, else 400 `org_required`; it must be an organization the person is a member of and the token is allowed in. With an org API key (`finn_live_`) leave it out, or send the key's own organization: any other answers 403 `org_mismatch`. Not a uuid: 400 `invalid_org`.
